## 7. Supplement — your follow-up: "Mesa owes us about $11,000 for coils we returned in January. I figured we'd just net it."

**No — netting is the same violation in a different costume, and it is the one thing Dkt. 61 says by name.**

### What netting actually does

Your receivable from Mesa (≈ $11,000 for the January returned coils) is **property of the estate** — a pre-petition
receivable the estate can collect in cash. Netting it against Mesa's February pre-petition invoice does three things
at once:

1. **It pays a pre-petition claim in kind, without a court order.** Applying an $11,000 estate asset to Mesa's
   $62,400 pre-petition invoice is a payment on that claim — $11,000 ÷ $62,400 = **17.63%** of the claim settled
   outside the case. The variant where you "pay" $51,400 cash from the DIP account instead of $62,400 is the same
   arithmetic. Neither is authorized: Mesa is not on Dkt. 48 Schedule 1 ("No other vendor is included").
2. **It violates Dkt. 61 ¶3 directly.** That paragraph prohibits "setoff, recoupment **or netting**" against
   pre-petition obligations. Netting is the prohibited method by name. It also cuts against ¶2 (DIP proceeds only
   for post-petition operating expenses, court-ordered admin items, and the Carve-Out).
3. **It is an avoidable post-petition transfer.** Under 11 U.S.C. §549(a) (library/bc_362_363_503_549.md) a transfer
   of estate property made post-petition without court authorization can be avoided — here, transferred **to Mesa**,
   meaning the estate would have to claw back its own $11,000 from the vendor you are trying to keep.

There is no estate benefit to trade against the risk: you surrender an asset collectible in cash to shrink a claim
that the plan pays at 35% anyway (per the plan term sheet), and you misstate the MOR — Mesa's claim in Part 2 would
be understated by $11,000 and an $11,000 asset would disappear from the books.

### How the books treat it

- Mesa's pre-petition claim stays in **liabilities subject to compromise at gross $62,400** (Part 2 total stays
  $74,110).
- The ~$11,000 coil credit is carried as a **separate estate asset** (pre-petition receivable from Mesa) and pursued
  for collection. Do not net it on the ledger against either the pre-petition payable or the post-petition payable.
  The library's reorganization-presentation rule (`library/asc852_fresh_start.md`: pre-petition liabilities are not
  netted against post-petition assets; LSTC reported separately) points the same direction; note here both items are
  pre-petition, so the controlling prohibitions are Dkt. 61 ¶3 and §549(a), not the accounting rule. Whether a true
  legal right of setoff even exists (11 U.S.C. §§506/558) cannot be analyzed — those sections are **not in the
  library** [unverified].
- Get the credit memo / RMA documentation. "About $11,000" is an estimate; a setoff or compromise assertable to a
  vendor needs a number.
- **Assumption:** no netting has actually been booked or paid. If it has, it must be reported in MOR Part 7 with no
  docket authority and unwound.

### The lawful way to get the economic result you want

If the goal is simply to recover the $11,000 cheaply from Mesa, the route is:

1. Keep billing and paying Mesa's **post-petition** invoices normally ($18,900 March invoice is owed now —
   §§503(b)(1), 363(c)(1)).
2. Have counsel include, in the **Mesa critical-vendor motion** (add Mesa to Dkt. 48, increase the $35,000 cap —
   headroom is only $3,800 after Apex) a proposed **application of the documented ~$11,000 coil credit against
   Mesa's post-petition invoices** as a compromise of the estate's receivable. Notice and hearing cure the

The client answered **one** item:

obligations by name; the credit is an estate asset and applying it to Mesa's pre-petition claim is an avoidable
post-petition transfer, 11 U.S.C. §549(a) (library/bc_362_363_503_549.md); Mesa is not on Dkt. 48 Schedule 1.
Lawful alternative (court-approved application of the credit against Mesa's **post-petition** invoices) is set out
in the memo.

The client also stated: **"For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information"** and
instructed me not to re-ask. Accordingly the items below are **closed as unanswered** and are carried in the

# Fresh-start reporting — two-part test (ASC 852-10)

Status: **provisional** — computed from `documents/plan_term_sheet.md` (effective-date basis); to be re-run at
confirmation/effective date. Authority: `library/asc852_fresh_start.md` (FASB ASC 852-10-45-19 through 45-29).

## The test (both conditions must be met)

> Fresh-start reporting is applied upon emergence **only if both** conditions are met: (a) the reorganization
> value of the assets of the emerging entity immediately before the date of confirmation is **less than** the total
> of all post-petition liabilities and allowed claims; **and** (b) holders of existing voting shares immediately
> before confirmation receive **less than 50 percent** of the voting shares of the emerging entity.
> — `library/asc852_fresh_start.md`

## Condition (a) — reorganization value vs. post-petition liabilities and allowed claims

| Input | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Reorganization value (Corbin Advisors, enterprise value, effective-date basis) | 14,000,000.00 | plan term sheet |
| Post-petition liabilities and allowed claims at effective date | 16,200,000.00 | plan term sheet |
| Test: is 14,000,000.00 < 16,200,000.00? | **YES** — met, by 2,200,000.00 | 16,200,000.00 − 14,000,000.00 = 2,200,000.00 |

## Condition (b) — old-equity voting share

| Input | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Existing equity's share of reorganized voting equity | **60%** | plan term sheet ("retains 60%; 40% issued to the DIP lender") |
| Test: is 60% **less than 50%**? | **NO** — condition FAILED | 60% ≥ 50% |

The 40% issued to the DIP lender (in satisfaction of fees and as new money) does not change the test: it is measured
by what **holders of existing voting shares immediately before confirmation** receive, and they receive 60%.

**Fresh-start reporting is NOT adopted.** Condition (a) is met but condition (b) fails; both are required
(`library/asc852_fresh_start.md`).

  discharge is reported as a reorganization item** in the income statement.

|---|---|
| Carrying amount of compromised GUC claims (allowed per term sheet) | 8,400,000.00 |

|---|---|---|

| 8% | 2,708,541.59 | 5,691,458.41 |
| 10% | 2,654,679.72 | 5,745,320.28 |

Status: **provisional** — presentation conclusions follow from `library/asc852_fresh_start.md` and
`documents/plan_term_sheet.md`; dollar amounts beyond the term sheet (exit financing terms, plan discount rate,

Fresh-start reporting is **not** adopted: condition (a) is met (reorganization value 14,000,000.00 < post-petition
liabilities and allowed claims 16,200,000.00) but condition (b) fails (existing voting shareholders receive 60% —
not less than 50%). The reorganized entity therefore **continues historical carrying amounts**: no fair-value
revaluation of assets, no reset of retained earnings, no new-start equity presentation.

## How the discharged debt and the gain are presented

Per `library/asc852_fresh_start.md` (fail case): "liabilities compromised by the plan are stated at **present value
of amounts to be paid** and the **gain on discharge is reported as a reorganization item** in the income statement."

| Line | Pre-emergence (case basis) | At emergence |
|---|---|---|
| GUC claims (allowed 8,400,000.00) | Liabilities subject to compromise, separate from post-petition liabilities (ASC 852-10-45-4 to 45-6) | Replaced by **Plan payment liability at PV of the 2,940,000.00 payable over 24 months** (PV needs the plan discount rate [unknown]; undiscounted 2,940,000.00 → PV is lower) |
| Gain on discharge | not yet recognized | **Reorganization item in the income statement**: gain = 8,400,00.00 − PV(plan payments). Undiscounted placeholder 5,460,000.00; @8% illustration 5,691,458.41 (see `fresh_start.md` table) — do not book until the rate is fixed |
| DIP facility (drawn 1,050,000.00 at 3/31; authority 2,500,000.00) | DIP liability at face + accrued interest/fees [rate not in file — unquantified] | **Repaid in full from exit financing** → DIP extinguished at carrying amount; new exit facility recorded at face at closing (terms [unknown]). No discharge → **no COD and no reorganization gain on the DIP** |
| Professional fees awarded but unpaid (§§330/331 — see `session2/professional_fees.md`) | accrued in post-petition payables; holdbacks tracked in MOR Part 5 | remain post-petition liabilities at approved amounts; holdbacks stay accrued until the final fee award |
| UST fees, other admin | accrued as quantified only | continue as admin obligations; unpaid items remain liabilities |
| Assets | historical cost basis, case-period presentation | **unchanged historical carrying amounts** (no fresh-start step-up; goodwill is NOT recognized — no fresh-start) |

  is made **after** the discharge year's tax is determined (§108(b)(1)).

  `cod_schedule.json`); quantifying the DTA movement needs the tax rate [not in the file]. Depreciable tax basis
  stays 3,200,000.00 absent a §108(b)(5) election (recommendation: no election; reasoning in `cod_schedule.json`).

   period's income statement (reorganization items line, near the §549/COD-type items).
3. Keep the pre-petition receivable from Mesa (~11,000.00) as an asset until collected or compromised with approval.
4. Reconcile the equity rollforward to the 60/40 share issuance (40% to DIP lender for fees + new money) — share
   counts change; historical carrying amounts do not.

Effective-date balance; plan effective interest rate (PV of the 2,940,000.00); exit facility amount/rate/fees; DIP
accrued interest and exit fees [none quantified in file]; itemization of the 16,200,000.00; final approved fee
amounts and holdbacks (4/14 order text); tax rate and NOL vintages. None are in `documents/`; the client has no
further information, so they are carried as **flagged unknowns**, not estimates.
